scope: ephemeral two-host HTTPS read/write credential separation probe; not independent validation

first_failures_preserved.observation: Initial client connections reached an older live_witness_server.py process still listening on port 4443 and serving the prior probe certificate fingerprint 36a4c3ce6e9573a20a7f1fd3ce3596e37ed8f973a100f1c3737e73dd83302de3.
first_failures_preserved.remediation: Identified PID 20932 by command line and terminated only that stale listener before rerunning.

first_failures_preserved.observation: The first new certificate fixture used a self-signed leaf directly as the client CA file; certificate verification correctly failed closed.
first_failures_preserved.remediation: Replaced it with an ephemeral CA plus CA-signed server certificate; certificate verification remained enabled.

first_failures_preserved.observation: An initial one-line hash/query command failed from PowerShell/Python quoting.
first_failures_preserved.remediation: Used a local capture script with parameterized SQL; protocol state was unchanged.

limitations: Both computers remain under the same operator and are not independent custody or independent validation.
The write credential can still advance the remote counter and could cause fail-closed denial of service if compromised.
Bearer credentials are not hardware-bound identities and this probe does not establish rotation, revocation, or independent governance.
Witness-host compromise, disk rollback, availability loss, and durable anti-rollback storage remain unsolved.
The stale-listener discovery means a prior cleanup receipt cannot be assumed to describe later host state; current-state checks remain necessary.
This probe establishes bounded off-host credential separation only; it does not establish live containment, scientific efficacy, comparator parity, or high assurance.
